findings.title: Reject ambiguous highest-priority crypto providers
findings.body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200, so sorting does not resolve a classpath containing more than one of these providers. The first service-loader entry is silently selected instead of the previous initialization failure. In particular, a classpath containing both the default and FIPS providers can select the non-FIPS implementation based on classpath order. Reject ties at the highest priority, or introduce an explicit selection mechanism, so an ambiguous configuration cannot silently use the wrong cryptographic implementation.

findings.title: Provide a compatible default for the new provider method
findings.body: Adding order() as an abstract method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations: their source no longer compiles, and previously compiled implementations can throw AbstractMethodError when the new provider comparator invokes order(). This also prevents selection of a valid built-in provider when an older custom provider is discovered alongside it. A default implementation would allow existing providers to remain loadable while the built-in providers override their priorities.

findings.title: Generate the appropriate EC curve for each algorithm
findings.body: Every test generates a key using the JCA provider's default EC curve, which is normally P-256. Selecting SHA384withECDSA or SHA512withECDSA does not change that key's curve, so the ES384 and ES512 tests only pad P-256 signature components to larger output sizes. They never exercise actual P-384 or P-521 signatures, including the long-form DER sequence length needed for P-521. Initialize the key generator with the algorithm's corresponding curve and verify that the reconstructed DER signature validates the original data, rather than only comparing two conversions performed by the same implementation.
